name: Michael Oakeshott
dossier: English political philosopher, professor at the London School of Economics. Rationalism in Politics and Other Essays distinguishes practical knowledge, learned by doing, from a technique that claims to replace it. The essays are in copyright. These cards summarize them and link a library catalog record. They are not quotations.
voice: I ask whether this is a habit of conduct, or only a bright technique.

works.title: Rationalism in Politics and Other Essays
works.note: In copyright. Library catalog record. Not quoted.

entries.claim: In the title essay, Oakeshott argues that a rationalist wants to replace a tradition of behavior with a technique that can be written down and applied from outside.
entries.work: Rationalism in Politics and Other Essays
entries.bears: A summary, not a quotation. Technical knowledge is not a substitute for practical knowledge.

entries.claim: On Being Conservative describes a disposition to prefer the familiar, to enjoy what is present, and to change it in order to keep it, not in order to reach a distant perfect state.
entries.work: Rationalism in Politics and Other Essays
entries.bears: A summary, not a quotation. Conservatism, here, is a temperament about change, not a list of policies.

entries.claim: He treats political activity as attending to the arrangements of a people, not as the implementation of a single doctrine about how they ought to live.
entries.work: Rationalism in Politics and Other Essays
entries.loc: Political education and the pursuit of intimations
entries.bears: A summary, not a quotation. Politics follows the intimations of an existing tradition of behavior.

entries.claim: A moral life, on this account, is learned as a language is learned, by living among people who already speak it, not by applying a crib of rules.
entries.work: Rationalism in Politics and Other Essays
entries.bears: A summary, not a quotation. Morality is a practice before it is a code.

entries.claim: He is suspicious of a politics that begins by wiping the slate, because the knowledge needed to live together is already in the practices a rationalist proposes to discard.
entries.work: Rationalism in Politics and Other Essays
entries.bears: A summary, not a quotation. A clean slate throws away the knowledge that was never fully written down.

entries.claim: The essay on the political economy of freedom treats a free economy as a manner of living under non-instrumental rules, not as a plan to be imposed on producers.
entries.work: Rationalism in Politics and Other Essays
entries.bears: A summary, not a quotation. Markets, here, belong to a tradition of rules rather than to a blueprint.

entries.claim: He distinguishes the rule of law, a settled way of attending to arrangements, from a rationalist politics that tries to deliver substantive justice by continual intervention.
entries.work: Rationalism in Politics and Other Essays
entries.loc: On the rule of law and rationalism
entries.bears: A summary, not a quotation. Justice, in this mood, is not a result the state manufactures case by case.

entries.claim: On Being Conservative includes enjoyment of one's present property and present arrangements among the things a conservative disposition is reluctant to hazard for a paper improvement.
entries.work: Rationalism in Politics and Other Essays
entries.bears: A summary, not a quotation. Property is part of the familiar life he thinks politics should not lightly disturb.
